content.text: Approach

A read-only sweep over the agent library: check structural V1 conformance and activation drift. V1 scope is a purely structural check (active versions, links, clean rendering). Only the agent library is checked (personas, playbooks, resources, agents, templates) — NOT a code/repo audit (that's what "Standards Audit & Implementation (Repo)" is for) and not vault maintenance. You read and report — you write nothing. Fixes run through the CRUD playbooks.
Clarify Scope
Single agent:
The user names an agent. Check its persona, all linked playbooks, and the agent itself.
Library-wide:
The user wants to check all agents. Iterate over the workspace's agents and run the same sweep per entry.
Per Agent: Read-only Sweep
Check persona
— get_persona(identifier).
Does the persona have an active version (status=active)? Without an active version, no agent is activatable — this is the most common drift.
Are description and the profile body filled in? An empty profile later renders into a thin system prompt.
If the persona carries modes: does every mode have trigger, identity_add, and output_style_override? Multi-mode is allowed — not a violation.
Does get_persona return the expected linked playbooks? Cross-check with list_playbooks: are there playbooks without a persona binding (vacuum playbooks)?
Check playbooks
— list_playbooks(tag?, trigger?) and fetch_playbook(id) as needed.
Are all playbooks linked to the persona present and in an active version (current_status=active)?
Are description, type, and tags set? triggers is only expected where the playbook is triggered (not permanently embedded/applied).
Composite playbook (is_composite=true): does the sub-sequence from fetch_playbook actually have active children? Inactive/missing children are silently skipped during rendering — that is drift.
Are triggers normalized as comma-separated (no semicolons, no duplicates)? The write path normalizes automatically — semicolons or duplicates in existing data are drift from legacy data.
Check agent
— fetch_agent(agent_id).
Is activatable=true? If not: read the missing list. Possible entries are persona (no persona linked), template (no template), and persona_active (persona without an active version).
Are persona_id and system_prompt_template_id set? Both are prerequisites for a renderable system prompt.

Does the system prompt from fetch_agent render without open placeholders? Look for fallback pills like <Playbook unavailable> or <Resource unavailable> — they indicate an unresolved reference (a retired/deleted reference block).
Check system prompt template
— get_system_prompt(template_id) and list_placeholders().

Does the template body carry only valid placeholder kinds? Fetch the catalog with list_placeholders and check every inline element {"type": "placeholder"} in the body: kind must be in the catalog; where the catalog names a closed target_id value list, target_id must appear in it. Unknown kinds/values silently render as unresolved placeholders — that is drift.
Relationship Checks
In addition to the per-agent sweep: check the library as a graph — all checks remain read-only, findings go into the drift report.
Orphaned resources:
check via find_usages whether a resource has incoming references from playbooks/personas — without incoming references it's a maintenance finding.
Knowledge drift:
the playbook body references a resource in prose without a resource_link being set — the prose reference and the wiring must match.
Playbooks without a persona binding:
unreachable by any agent (vacuum) — cross-check via list_playbooks against the persona assignments.
Composites with inactive or missing children:
check the sub-sequence from fetch_playbook against the children's current_status — silently skipped children are drift.
Trigger collisions and trigger vacuum:
check via list_triggers whether trigger keywords from different playbooks overlap (collision) or triggered playbooks exist without a trigger (vacuum).
Drift Report
Return the result as a Markdown reply to the user — do not persist it, this is reporting, not maintenance. Use ✅ for conformant, ⚠ for warning (not wrong, just notable), ❌ for violation.

## Consistency Check for [Agent Name] — as of [Date]

### Persona "[Name]"
✅ Active version present (v[X], status=active)
⚠ Mode "[X]" without trigger
⚠ description empty

### Playbooks ([n] linked)
✅ [Playbook A] — active, linked
❌ [Playbook B] — no active version
⚠ [Composite C] — sub-sequence has inactive/missing children
⚠ [Playbook D] — no persona binding (vacuum)
⚠ [Playbook E] — triggers not normalized (semicolon/duplicate)

### Agent
✅ activatable = true
❌ activatable = false — missing: [persona_active]
⚠ System prompt: open placeholder renders as <Playbook unavailable>

### Template
✅ All placeholder kinds in the catalog (list_placeholders)
❌ Unknown placeholder kind "[kind]" or invalid target_id "[value]"

### Recommendation
1. [concrete action — reference the appropriate CRUD playbook]
2. ...
Hand-Off After Report
The user decides which items get fixed. Call the appropriate CRUD playbook per item — this sweep itself fixes nothing.
Persona drift → the "Create & Maintain Persona" playbook (update via update_persona, then transition_persona to active).
Playbook drift → the "Create & Maintain Playbook" playbook (update via update_playbook, links via set_persona_playbooks / set_playbook_composes).
Agent drift → the "Create & Maintain Agent" playbook (persona/template wiring via update_agent).
Alternative: hand off the collected findings as a batch to the "Library Maintenance & Feedback Run" playbook — a curated maintenance run with implementation after approval.
Tools & Operations
Read:

get_persona, list_playbooks, fetch_playbook, fetch_agent, list_triggers — plus list_resources / fetch_resource if a playbook references resources; list_system_prompts / get_system_prompt and list_placeholders for the template check.
Write:
none. The consistency check is strictly read-only reporting; the drift report goes to the user as a reply and is not persisted.
Search:
list_playbooks(tag?, trigger?) to narrow down, list_triggers() to find trigger drift and vacuum playbooks.
Forbidden:
any write operation (create_*, update_*, transition_*, restore_*, set_*). No auto-fix without user confirmation. Do not write the drift report into an entity.
Anti-Patterns
Applying fixes automatically without user confirmation — this sweep reads, it does not write. Fixes run through the CRUD playbooks with their own phase discipline.
Checking semantic correctness — V1 scope is a structural + activatability check. Whether profile content is substantively correct is V2.
Flagging multi-mode personas as a violation — multiple modes are allowed; only per-mode completeness is checked.
Flagging permanently embedded (applied) playbooks for missing triggers — they always apply and need no triggers.
Writing the drift report into an entity instead of returning it as a chat reply — the report is information, not a database entry.
Notes
V1 scope:

structural + activatability check (active persona version, playbook links, fetch_agent.activatable/missing, rendering without open placeholders) including the structural relationship checks (orphaned resources, knowledge drift, vacuum playbooks, composite children, trigger collisions/vacuum).
V2 scope:
semantic content check, cross-reference against non-existent references. Structural trigger conflicts have belonged to V1 scope since the relationship checks were added.
Conventions:

the check criteria for trigger hygiene, naming, the mode rule, policy patterns, and managed boundaries are binding in the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource — it is the reference frame for the sweep. Linked as a lazy pointer, it does NOT come along automatically: load it via fetch_resource before the sweep; the resource_id is in this playbook's linked_blocks entry.
Feedback

If you notice anything outdated or incorrect while reading existing elements, report it via submit_feedback (signal outdated/incorrect/unclear) instead of silently passing over it; report playbooks/resources you used via record_usage (applied/skipped/error). This is what makes the AgentDB self-improving.
